exitStory.y5Lead: The single number this section drives. Investors use it (× the sector exit multiple ÷ their target ROI) to back-solve the pre-money you can credibly defend.
exitStory.y5Desc: What you realistically expect to bill in your fifth full year. Use the sector default below as a starting point, then sharpen it once your traction or market sizing is firmer.
exitStory.sectorDefaultHint: (typical Y5 ARR for {sector} at this stage)
exitStory.investorAskLead: What return multiple does the fund need to justify the check? This is the fund-side hurdle, not your own ROI.
exitStory.targetRoiDesc: The higher the number, the lower your pre-money. {roi}× means the investor wants €{roi} back for every €1 they put in today — typically 7–10 years later, after several rounds of dilution. Pre-seed ~30×, seed ~20×, Series A ~10×. We pre-filled {roi}× for {stage}.

round.kindTitle: What kind of round are you raising?
round.kindLead: This choice changes what we can show in the preview.
round.kindLeadDetail: Priced equity: we model this close immediately — new investors receive raise ÷ post-money (see the bar below). That percentage is not the same as the cumulative dilution-to-exit field further up. SAFEs and convertibles convert at the next priced round, so there is no fixed ownership slice here yet.
round.preMoneyTargetDesc: Leave blank to use the blended valuation from the steps above. Only fill in if you have already agreed a pre-money with a lead investor.
round.dilutionDesc: Expected total founder dilution through exit (median benchmarks — Atomico State of European Tech 2024 · Dealroom Benelux 2024). We start from {pct}% for {stage}. It does not drive the bar chart: this round’s new-investor % is always raise ÷ post-money.
round.useStageDefaultAria: Reset cumulative exit dilution to the {stage} median default of {pct}%
round.optionPoolDesc: Equity reserved for future hires. Most rounds use 10–15%; investors often expect this to be visible in the pre-money stack.
round.capTableExplainer: Ownership after this close (pre-money + raise, with the option pool reserved). New investors ≈ {roundPct}% post-money from this raise alone — separate from the cumulative-to-exit % field.
round.roundDilutionHighHint: ~{roundPct}% for new money is a large slice for a single round; many founders aim closer to 10–15% per major cheque. At this raise, about 12% would correspond to pre-money near {preHint} (illustrative — use your actual term sheet).

prior_exit.title: Prior venture-backed exit (≥€10M)
prior_exit.description: Any cofounder has exited a previous venture-backed company at €10M+ enterprise value.
prior_exit.evidence: Investors verify: Crunchbase / Dealroom exit record, public press release, or LP reference.

top_unicorn_alumnus.title: Top-tier scaleup alumnus
top_unicorn_alumnus.description: Any cofounder spent ≥2 years at senior level (senior IC, lead, manager, staff or above — not entry-level / intern) inside a Benelux or European top-tier scaleup (Adyen, Showpad, Collibra, Bol, Mollie, UiPath, Klarna, Wise, Spotify…).
top_unicorn_alumnus.evidence: Investors verify: LinkedIn tenure + role band; many funds maintain a "mafia" graph of these networks.

domain_expert_10y.title: 10+ years industry experience
domain_expert_10y.description: Any cofounder has 10+ years operating experience inside the target customer's industry — founder-market fit beats generic founder strength at pre-seed.
domain_expert_10y.evidence: Investors verify: prior employer references; reverse interviews with target customers asking "would you buy from this person?"

second_time_founder.title: Second-time founder
second_time_founder.description: Any cofounder previously founded a company that operated for ≥2 years (no exit required — the "I shipped a company" signal alone is meaningful).
second_time_founder.evidence: Investors verify: KBO/KVK incorporation history, prior cap table, GitHub or product archives.

has_technical_cofounder.title: Full-time technical cofounder
has_technical_cofounder.description: At least one full-time technical cofounder owns the codebase end-to-end. Mitigates the most common pre-seed execution risk (outsourced engineering).
has_technical_cofounder.evidence: Investors verify: equity split, GitHub commits, technical due diligence interview.

solo_founder.title: Solo founder (no cofounders)
solo_founder.description: Single founder operating without cofounders. Solo founders close at materially lower pre-money in published Benelux datasets — the discount is empirical, not a judgment.
solo_founder.evidence: Picking this clears the technical-cofounder lift — both can't be true at once.

inceptionLens.heading: Inception lens (optional)
inceptionLens.subline: For founders who aren't on a conventional milestone path. Acknowledges that pre-seed is won by momentum (not moats) and that the best founders cost more. Default: off.
inceptionLens.whatLensBody: It lifts the mid (engine output) AND widens the band (lower P10, higher P90). Honest about increased variance — no false precision. Canonical math comes from ValuationIQ; this lens is a published, peer-reviewed overlay (Hampus Jakobsson 2024 inception thesis, Atomico SoEU 2024).

milestones_driven.title: Milestones-driven
milestones_driven.subtitle: Standard pre-seed: measurable milestones, peer-comparable trajectory. Conventional Berkus + Scorecard + VC blend, no overlay.

momentum_driven.title: Momentum-driven
momentum_driven.subtitle: "Pre-seed is won by momentum, not moats." Inbound investor interest, hiring acceleration, early customer pull. Lift +10%, ±15% wider variance band.
momentum_driven.examples: Right when peers reach out unprompted; team scaling 2× per quarter; users asking for the next version.

inception_bet.title: Inception bet
inception_bet.subtitle: Edge premium + market-creation thesis. Spike profile, generational ambition, no ceiling. Lift +25%, ±25% wider variance band — high variance, asymmetric upside acknowledged honestly.
inception_bet.examples: The Lovable / Anthropic / Cursor profile. Borderline insane ambition, technical or distribution spike, market-creating thesis.

methodology.heading: Three frameworks, one defensible number
methodology.lede: We blend three valuation methods angel investors and seed funds actually ask about. Each is grounded in published research — no proprietary black box.

cards.title: Berkus method
cards.body: Five risk-reduction milestones (idea, prototype, team, partnerships, rollout). Each milestone earns a defined contribution toward the pre-money — anchored on stage-aware ceilings, not a point-in-time gut feel.

cards.title: Bill Payne Scorecard
cards.attribution: Bill Payne / Frontier Angels — published methodology, 2024 update
cards.body: Five weighted factors (market size, defensibility, GTM, capital efficiency, other tailwinds) compared against the regional median. The result is a multiplier on a published Benelux baseline.

cards.title: VC method
cards.body: Year-5 revenue × an exit-EV/revenue multiple ÷ the fund's target ROI. Surfaces the "what does the fund need to see" lens that priced rounds actually solve for.

sources.heading: Calibrated against published research
sources.lede: Benchmarks are not invented. The numbers the engine compares your inputs against come from public datasets:
sources.note: Sources are cited inline in your downloaded report wherever a benchmark drives a number.

items.q: Why is the wizard free without signing up?
items.a: Filling it gives you a number you can paste into a deck on its own — that's already useful, with or without the PDF. Signup is only for the polished investor-ready report and to keep your work across sessions.

items.q: How accurate is this versus a paid valuation?
items.a: It's a triangulation across three established methods, not a single ground-truth number. For a term sheet or a SAFE conversion, your accountant should sign off the cap table — we make that a one-click invite from inside the report.

items.q: What happens to my inputs if I leave without signing up?
items.a: They stay in your browser only (localStorage). Nothing is sent to our servers until you sign up. If you come back within 24 hours, your inputs reload automatically.

items.q: Can I run this for a non-Belgian / non-Dutch startup?
items.a: The wizard works for any company — the regional benchmarks today are calibrated for Belgium and the Netherlands. If you're elsewhere in Europe, the numbers still triangulate but you should treat the regional multiplier as approximate.
